description: Change the shared memory (a tree of folders and .json files; same paths as the memory tool, keep the file extension). Each op also updates the index, so you never edit _index.json yourself. Examples: {"op":"add","path":"notes/amy.json","value":"Amy likes tea.","description":"Who Amy is"} makes a new file ; {"op":"add","path":"notes/people.json#/bob","value":{"likes":"tea"},"description":"Who Bob is"} adds key bob inside notes/people.json (that file must hold an object, for example made with value {}) ; {"op":"add","path":"notes/trips/","description":"Trips"} makes a folder (path ends with /) ; {"op":"set","path":"notes/amy.json","value":"Amy likes coffee."} replaces the value (description optional) ; {"op":"rm","path":"notes/amy.json"} deletes it (a folder that is not empty needs "recursive":true). Keep one text value under 2 KB; split bigger ones into keys or files. Errors: NodeExists (use set), NodeMissing (the line lists what exists), ValueBad, PathBad (writing outside the memory, or the root), ChildrenExist, TargetBad, WriteFailed (read-only for you).

op.description: add = create something new; set = change something that exists; rm = delete

path.description: Like notes/amy.json, notes/amy.json#/phone or notes/trips/ (ends with / = a folder). Relative to the memory root; copy paths as the memory tool prints them.

value.description: add/set: the content, any JSON (text is a string). For a file that is not .json it must be a string. At most 8000 bytes.

description.description: One line saying what this is; required for add, optional for set. Shown in the index.

recursive.description: rm: also delete a folder that is not empty.
